title.en: On an Autumn Night, to Qiu the Twenty-second

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died around 792.
basis.zh: 唐诗，作者约卒于 792 年。

note.en: Wei Yingwu wrote it to his friend Qiu Dan, who had gone to live as a recluse in the mountains. Half the poem is where the poet is and half is where the friend is, and the falling pine cone joins them: he imagines the sound in the friend’s silence and guesses that the friend is awake too. It is one of the shortest poems about friendship across distance, and one of the truest.
note.zh: 韦应物写给友人丘丹，丘丹当时隐居山中。诗一半写自己所在，一半写朋友所在，一颗落下的松子把两边连起来：他想象朋友那边的寂静里松子落地的声音，猜想朋友此刻也还醒着。这是写远方友情最短的诗之一，也是最真的之一。

excerpt.orig: 山空松子落，幽人應未眠。
excerpt.en: The mountain is empty; a pine cone falls. / The one who lives there, I think, is not yet asleep.
excerpt.zh: 山空松子落，幽人应未眠。

gloss.en: 屬: it happens to be, just at.
Chanting poems in the cool air.
gloss.zh: 咏：吟诵。凉天：秋夜清凉的天气。

gloss.en: Qiu the Twenty-second, Qiu Dan, had left office and was studying the Way on Linping Mountain near Hangzhou; pine seeds were said to be the food of immortals.
gloss.zh: 丘二十二即丘丹，曾任员外郎，当时在临平山隐居学道。传说松子是仙人的食物。

note.en: A delicate act of imagining, a pine cone falling in a friend’s silence; as pure as Wang Wei, though slighter in substance.
note.zh: 想象细腻：松子落在友人的寂静里；清幽不输王维，只是分量更轻。
